evidence:
CORE BEHAVIOUR GRADED: the brief's defining behaviours each have functional criteria, several at weight 2. These include one-stage moves, shared order, Interview places, stale-move refusal naming who, all-or-none multi-move, undo, the live board, conversations/unread/seen/drafts and candidate privacy (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: hro_move_one_stage w1.5, hro_reorder w1.5, hro_stale_refused w2, hro_bulk_all_or_none w2, hro_undo_restores w2, hro_live_board w2, hro_unread_counts w2, hro_drafts w2, hro_candidate_private w2).

SERVER-BACKED, NOT SAME-ORIGIN: the constraints gate hro_gate_shared (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml) adds a card through the UI, reloads, then reads the card as the Observer in a new independent browser context ('A static seed response, a no-op success message or a browser-only save does not satisfy the gate'). Constraints prompt.md line 22 rules out a reload or a second tab as an independent context. The same check is the global browser gate in functional prompt.md line 11 and polish prompt.md line 11. Mei Lin re-reads shared order in independent contexts (functional prompt.md protocols M/B; hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder, hro_add_candidate, hro_job_open). Per-person unread is read in Mei's own session (hro_unread_counts), and seen marks are checked across contexts (hro_seen). The gate stays simple (load, reload, server-backed), as lesson 4 advises.

RESTART DURABILITY (lesson 15): protocol D (functional prompt.md line 59) records jobs, card order per stage, notes, last messages, per-conversation unread counts, activity lines and the seeded Platform Engineer order and note. It then calls restart_app once, signs in again in a fresh independent context and compares. hro_restart (w1.5, last criterion in judge.toml) fails if anything is lost, reordered or duplicated, or if the seed is loaded again. By then many revisions exist: J1/J2 with 11+ cards, repeated reorders, moves and undos, several notes, the T/U messages and the activity lines. restart_app is a real process-group kill and relaunch over the same DB_PATH as uid 65534 (tests/test.sh lines 127-193, identical to the template) and is single-use (restart_mcp.py lines 29-31). The seed expectations match environment/assets/seed_data.json: PLAT Applied Greta/Ade/Marco, Screen Priya/Samuel, and the APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'.

LESSON 16 (no double grading): hro_restart compares against the record taken before the restart, so a feature that never worked earlier is not deducted again. The seeded order/note check appears only in hro_restart (a grep for 'Greta' hits only that row and protocol Z), so it is not graded twice.

RE-AUTH AND BROWSER-LOCAL STATE: the brief lets drafts live anywhere on 'that browser'. Reload and switching conversations are graded in hro_drafts (functional). The polish row hro_pol_session_resume (w2) grades three things: a session ending mid-reply, the reply resuming after sign-in, and another person on the same browser not seeing reply or note drafts.

BROKEN APPS TRIED: (a) A board stored only in localStorage fails the gate, because the Observer reads from an independent context. (b) An in-memory server store passes the gate but loses hro_restart, and the D comparison catches a reseed on boot. (c) If read markers live only in memory, Rafael's opened conversations show unread again after the restart, so hro_restart fails. (d) Reseeding on every start, which duplicates jobs, fails 'starting data is not loaded again' and the duplication check. None of these passes.

CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE TRIED: an app with per-tab sessions, SSE or polling and any route layout. The gate and D use UI sign-in and fresh contexts, not routes, so this app is not penalised. Minor P3 observation: D asks the judge to record 'the last messages of your conversations' and 'your unread count per conversation'. Suppose a judge reads the counts first and then opens conversations to read their last messages. Opening legitimately marks them read, and that persists, so the counts after the restart would differ from the recorded ones and a conforming app could be marked down. The listed order (messages before counts) keeps the literal reading consistent, so this is not a Fail. Wording such as 'record unread counts after reading the last messages, or without opening any conversation' would remove the ambiguity.

RUNTIME: in the scripted golden driver (not a judge run), group 24 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages, unread counts and activity without reseeding; live updates resume' PASSES (results/workspace.json, via-solve.log line 26; workspace.cjs lines 539-550 do a real SIGTERM and relaunch). RISK=true because there is no full configured functional judge run (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... and Oracle/target scores are absent'). Two things are unmeasured. First, whether the judge reaches protocol D, which runs LAST after protocols Z..A within timeout=9000. Second, whether hro_restart scores 1 on the golden. If the budget runs out, hro_restart is NOT EXERCISED and scores 0.
